summary: Feed s095_single to IDS is degraded: 9.5% of frames are truncated/sliced to ~128 bytes (168/1770, threshold 5%), all other checks healthy. Slicing removes payload the IDS needs for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snap-length is enabled at ~128 bytes, likely to conserve bandwidth to the 1 Gbps IDS port. 168 of 1770 frames (9.49%) are cut short, stripping L4/L7 payload before delivery.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true for signature matching and stream reassembly. Truncated frames hide exploits, prevent file/malware extraction and cause missed detections/false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload up to 1518 bytes; disable slicing or set snaplen >=1518/MTU so complete packets reach the IDS for full detection coverage.
